sheets.noticed: Bold white condensed type on a blueprint-blue grid: 'SOMEONE STEALS YOUR PASSWORD.' A strong, plain hook. Still in.
'CAN'T GET IN.' appears under the same sentence, so the hook carries on. Still in, though it is just text so far.
'They still can't get in.' is repeated on screen for about two seconds with no visuals. I am getting restless but I want the 'why'. Still in.
'Here's why.' then 'Logging in asks for two things' on the same blue. Still text only, but the promise of an answer keeps me. Still in.
The first real visual: a PASSWORD card under 'SOMETHING YOU KNOW'. The diagram finally gives my eyes something. Still in.
A PHONE card joins the password under 'SOMETHING YOU HAVE'. Two-factor now reads clearly as two keys. Still in.
'THIEF' drops in while the two cards sit at the top. Now there is a character, so there is a story. Still in.
A labeled arrow points from THIEF to the password. 'THE SITE' appears beside it. Clear and easy to follow. Still in.
THE SITE sends a CODE arrow to the phone card. The flow is easy to see at a glance. Still in.
The code path is shown again and 'WHICH THE THIEF DOESN'T HAVE' comes up. The diagram is repeating itself a little. Still in.
A dim 'THIEF'S LOGIN' box appears and the thief is stopped. The visual payoff of the blocked login holds me. Still in.
'STILL LOCKED' pops in with 'ONE STOLEN KEY ISN'T ENOUGH.' The point is clear and tidy. Still in.
'THEY'D NEED BOTH.' lands big over the locked state. A clean ending I would not swipe away from. Still in.
The last frame holds the full diagram with 'THEY'D NEED BOTH.' and the clip ends. I would stay until the end card.

remembers: Someone steals your password, but with two-factor login they still can't get in. Logging in asks for something you know, your password, plus something you have, your phone, so the site's code to your phone stops the thief. One stolen key isn't enough; they'd need both.
